summary: Request: reversible pseudonymization SIEM export using customer-supplied KEK-split and resumable hourly manifests
description:
Issue summary: ClearPath Bank (enterprise) requests a tenant-scoped SIEM export that supports reversible pseudonymization using a customer-supplied key-encryption-key (KEK) split across escrow holders. They require hourly export bundles to an S3 bucket with a per-bundle signed manifest and a resumable cursor (resume_token) so they can reliably replay and resume interrupted transfers. Impact: customer compliance team cannot complete their GDPR / SAR testing without reversible pseudonymization that can be unwrapped under escrow conditions and auditable per-file integrity proofs.

Request details:
- Export cadence: hourly bundles by tenant (UTC) for the last 90 days.
- Output format: newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON), with a manifest.json per hour listing files, event counts, ISO8601 window, per-file HMAC (sha256) and object size.
- Pseudonymization: field-level reversible pseudonymization for PII fields (email, user_id, ip_address) using envelope encryption where the data key is encrypted with a KEK provided by the customer.
- KEK delivery: customer will provide KEK material that must be split using a 2-of-3 Shamir-like split for escrow across their security team, Redwood security, and an external auditor. Redwood must store only the KEK shares needed for service (not the full KEK), and must produce an attestation of key-splitting operations.
- Resume semantics: each manifest must include a resume_token that encodes a high-water mark for each tenant; if a transfer fails, the customer wants an idempotent resume API to request the next chunk.
- Deletion/SAR support: for subject access or deletion, Redwood must provide a deletion-proof token and an auditable log entry mapping pseudonymized identity -> deletion action and timestamp.

Security constraints:
- All exports must be encrypted in transit (HTTPS/mTLS) and at rest (AES-256 server-side encryption with customer-provided keys supported via KMS).
- Per-file HMAC must be computed using a per-tenant signing key derived from the KEK and included in manifest.

comments: 2026-03-10 10:12 - Asha Mehta (Support): Opened ticket after call with ClearPath Bank compliance. Customer prefers implementation using customer-supplied KEK with split escrow. Asked for initial engineering feasibility review and security sign-off.

2026-03-10 13:40 - Liam O'Connor (Engineering): Acknowledged. Requesting clarification on whether the customer expects Redwood to hold any single full KEK material, and whether 2-of-3 shares are acceptable for our compliance team. Also asked if the HMAC key derivation can be standard HKDF-SHA256 from the wrapper key.

2026-03-11 09:05 - ClearPath Bank (Customer): Confirmed they will not allow Redwood to hold the full KEK. 2-of-3 split is acceptable. They can provide guidance on escrow providers. They prefer per-tenant HKDF-SHA256 for HMAC key derivation. They also requested an attestation that Redwood's KMS supports import-wrapped keys or CEP (customer-encrypted payload) patterns.

2026-03-11 15:22 - Security (internal): Noted regulatory review needed for storing key shares and escrow process. Asked product to provide threat model and proposed key handling flow. Added label 'security-review-required'.

2026-03-12 08:30 - Liam O'Connor (Engineering): Added implementation sketch: (1) Accept encrypted KEK shares via SFTP to a secure ingest bucket with strict ACLs; (2) Store each share in a hardware-backed keystore with access policies; (3) Use envelope encryption per-record: generate ephemeral data key (DEK), encrypt PII fields with DEK, wrap DEK with reconstructed KEK during allowed 'unwrap' operations; (4) Emit hourly NDJSON bundles to customer's S3 with manifest.json and resume_token. Asked infra for ETA and whether KMS import API supports split-keystore flow.
investigation_notes: Preliminary engineering review: feasible but requires changes to siem-bridge and audit-export pipeline. Key questions: how to handle live rotation of KEK shares and emergency escrow recovery; whether we can reuse existing KMS import APIs or need new codepath for 'split-keystore' semantics. Potential implementation risks: accidental full KEK reconstruction in memory, increased blast radius if key shares are compromised, and additional compliance documentation for escrow holders. Logged a tech spike request to prototype resume_token format (cursor includes tenant_id + last_event_seq + bundle_window).
resolution_notes: Pending - design review scheduled with Security, Product, and Infra on 2026-03-16. No customer-facing delivery yet. Next steps: (1) Security to approve key-splitting attestation language; (2) Engineering to create prototype siem-bridge PR for manifest+resume_token and per-file HMAC (linked PR created); (3) Product to update SLA/contract language for escrow storage and emergency unwrapping. Will update ticket with design doc link and prototype timeline after 2026-03-16 meeting.
workaround: Customer can continue using current full-audit exports with irreversible pseudonymization (hashing) while Redwood builds reversible flow. Note: irreversible hashes do not meet their SAR requirements.
